title: Walking Project: Social Media Communication & Website Redesign | Studio 1947
description: How Studio 1947 built bilingual social campaigns and a new website for Walking Project, Mumbai's citizen movement for safe, convenient and joyful walking.
ogTitle: Walking Project: Communication & Website Redesign | Studio 1947
ogDescription: Campaign design, data storytelling, and a website redesign for Mumbai's pedestrian advocacy movement.

hero.alt: The Walking Project mark: a pair of walking feet in white on a marigold yellow square

body: Walking Project is a citizen-led movement working to give everyone in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region a safe, convenient and joyful walk. Founded in 2012, the collective maps footpaths, audits pedestrian infrastructure, runs neighbourhood walkability teams across the city, and pushes civic bodies to build the sidewalks Mumbai's millions of walkers deserve. A minimum agenda for the maximum city.

Studio 1947 worked with Walking Project on two fronts: a social media system that turns footpath data into campaigns people feel and share, and a redesign of their website so a decade of advocacy reads as one clear, credible movement.

sections.heading: The Brief: Make Walkability Impossible to Ignore

sections.label: The Challenge
body: Nearly half of Mumbai moves on foot, yet pedestrians are the city's most invisible group. Walkability data sat in reports and spreadsheets: accurate, urgent, and unread. The movement needed posts that could stop a thumb mid-scroll, and a website that could hold the attention it won.
The work had to speak the city's languages, Hindi and Marathi first with English alongside, and stay instantly recognisable as Walking Project across every post, poster and page.

cards.title: From Data to Feeling
cards.body: Footpath statistics and road audits had to become images that carry emotion, not just information.

cards.title: A City's Own Languages
cards.body: Campaigns built Marathi-first and Hindi-first, so the message lands with the Mumbaikars who walk the most.

cards.title: One Recognisable Voice
cards.body: A repeatable visual system (marigold, signal red, bold Devanagari type) that reads as Walking Project at a glance.

sections.heading: The Campaign: चलने की आज़ादी है क्या?
sections.label: Social Media Communication
body: The anchor campaign asks one question: chalne ki azadi hai kya? Is there freedom to walk? Borrowing the charge of the word azadi, the series puts the people who actually walk Mumbai at its centre: an elderly woman on her evening round, a schoolgirl with her backpack, a senior citizen on his morning walk, each striding across a silhouette of the city's skyline.
Hand-drawn Devanagari display type does the shouting, the walkers do the convincing, and every poster closes with the same invitation: join the movement with Walking Project.

sections.heading: Numbers That Walk
sections.label: Data Storytelling
body: Walking Project's strongest asset is its evidence, so the feed treats statistics as heroes. 46% of Mumbaikars commute on foot. That number is set in oversized Devanagari numerals and asked back to the city in Marathi: Mumbaikars walk, but are our footpaths safe? The same layout ships in daylight blue and alarm red, so the fact returns to the feed without repeating itself.

A city-scale map drawn from open data makes the other number real: 2,000 kilometres of roads, and every line of it walked. Year-end recaps carry the movement's wins back to the community that made them happen, over duotone photographs of volunteers auditing the streets.

sections.heading: Two Colours, One Voice
sections.label: Visual Language
body: The identity runs on exactly two colours. The marigold of the mark: taxi-top yellow, traffic paint, high-visibility optimism. And the charcoal that carries the walking feet, the type and the city silhouette. Individual campaigns can change their backdrop, but the pair stays fixed, so every post reads as Walking Project before you read a single word.
Bold hand-lettered Devanagari headlines give the campaigns a protest-poster urgency, while clean grotesque body type keeps the data credible.

sections.heading: A Website That Holds the Argument
sections.label: Website Redesign
body: Social media wins the first three seconds. The website has to win the next three minutes. We rebuilt walkingproject.org around the movement's tagline, safe, convenient and joyful walking for all, leading with the one photograph that says everything: a Mumbai footpath at rush hour, full of people, beside a road full of cars.

The redesign sorts a decade of work (footpath audits, traffic island fixes, local walkability teams, press coverage) into a navigation a first-time visitor can walk through. Joining the movement and supporting it are always one click away.

cards.title: A movement that looks like one
cards.body: Posts, posters and the website now share one voice, so every audit and neighbourhood walk builds the same recognisable identity.

cards.title: Data people actually share
cards.body: Footpath statistics moved out of reports and into the feed, in the languages Mumbai walks and talks in.

cards.title: A clearer way in
cards.body: The redesigned site turns sympathy into membership: what Walking Project does, why it matters, and how to join are never more than a click apart.
